rounds.text: Nacdac Infrastructure Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive price-to-earnings ratio of just 5.76x compared to a sector benchmark of 12.64x [E1, E6]. The business demonstrates robust fundamental health, supported by a solid return on capital employed of 20.5% and a median return on equity of 20% over five years [E12, E21], both comfortably outpacing broader sector medians [E10, E56]. Long-term compounding remains exceptional, with 5-year sales growth at 57% and profit growth reaching 123% [E14, E17]. Furthermore, the valuation offers an extraordinary margin of safety, as a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at ₹148 per share against a market price of ₹21 [E38, E39], while a reverse DCF implies that the current price is pricing in an overly pessimistic -9.3% earnings growth [E40]. Conceded: the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], experiences a TTM sales contraction of -2% and profit contraction of -29% [E16, E19], and has seen operating margins trend downward over the last four years [E26].

Nacdac Infrastructure Ltd faces severe, structural margin compression that undermines its backward-looking valuation metrics [E26]. Operating margins have steadily decreased over the last four years [E26], falling to 7% in the trailing twelve months compared to 14% three years earlier, while quarterly operating margin dropped to 10% in September 2026 from 22% in the year-ago quarter [E24, E25]. This deterioration is translating into top and bottom-line contraction in the near term, with compounded sales growth dropping to -2% and compounded profit growth plunging to -29% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E19]. Compounded share price growth over the past year has collapsed by 45%, leaving the stock languishing at just 6% of its 52-week range [E5, E20]. Furthermore, despite reporting profits, the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% and generated negative free cash flow of Rs -0.99 Cr in March 2026 alongside rising borrowings of Rs 9.62 Cr [E4, E30, E32]. Institutional confidence has evaporated sharply, as foreign institutional holdings dropped from 9.50% in December 2024 to 1.60% in September 2026, and domestic institutional holdings fell completely from 4.95% to 0.00% over the same period [E35, E36]. Conceded: [E38] showing an intrinsic value of Rs 148 per share and an 85.8% margin of safety.

While the bear points to four-year operating margin compression [E26], the business maintains a robust historical growth profile with 57% compounded sales growth and 123% compounded profit growth over five years [E14, E17]. Conceded: operating margins dropped to 7% in TTM and 10% in Sep 2026 [E24, E25], and TTM sales and profit growth contracted by -2% and -29% [E16, E19]. However, this cyclical weakness ignores that profits remain fully backed by cash with a 1.71x cash conversion ratio for March 2026 [E28], alongside strong net profit and sales acceleration showing +83% and +231% YoY metrics [E47, E49]. The 45% share price decline and position at 6% of its 52-week range [E5, E20] overlook an intrinsic value gap offering an 85.8% margin of safety [E39], where current pricing absurdly implies -9.3% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E40]. Conceded: dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], free cash flow was negative at Rs -0.99 Cr [E30], borrowings rose to Rs 9.62 Cr [E32], and institutional holdings declined [E35, E36]. Yet debt-to-equity remains at a moderate 0.32x [E31], and promoters have actually increased their stake to 69.99% [E34], demonstrating insider commitment while the construction sector enjoys a supportive tailwind score [E51].

The bull highlights historical five-year growth of 57% in sales and 123% in profits [E14, E17], but concedes and downplays severe short-term deterioration, specifically a -2% sales contraction and a -29% profit decline over the trailing twelve months [E16, E19]. Conceded: the company shows strong short-term YoY sales and net profit acceleration [E47, E49]; however, this clashes directly with the broader multi-year trend of yearly operating margins decreasing continuously over the last four years [E26] and plunging down to 7% in the TTM and 10% in the recent quarter [E24, E25]. While the bull points to a 1.71x cash conversion ratio [E28], it glosses over the actual free cash flow sinking into negative territory at Rs -0.99 Cr [E30] alongside rising borrowings climbing to Rs 9.62 Cr [E32]. Conceded: promoters increased their stake slightly to 69.99% [E34]; nevertheless, institutional confidence has completely evacuated, marked by foreign institutions slashing holdings from 9.50% to 1.60% and domestic institutions entirely exiting from 4.95% to 0.00% [E35, E36]. Finally, invoking an 85.8% margin of safety and implied reverse DCF metrics [E38, E40] ignores the reality of the share price sitting at a mere 6% of its 52-week range after a punishing 45% one-year price drop [E5, E20] and a zero dividend yield [E4].
